Also read internal/service/result_measure.go (T1, measureResult) and internal/config/bounds.go (RetainedResultBounds) as the inputs you consume.

WRITE ONLY these nine paths: internal/service/result_handle.go (new), internal/service/result_handle_test.go (new), internal/observe/metrics.go, internal/observe/metrics_test.go, internal/observe/envelope.go, internal/observe/log_test.go, internal/observe/log.go (eventMessage registry: the twelve new §7 event entries, closed set), internal/observe/httpdiagnostics.go (operationVocabulary to R12's frozen 31 values), docs/logging-contract.md (log field vocabulary only; the config-codes block is T1's and must not be touched). T2 is store-only and handler-free: no retrieve_result dispatch, no inbound wiring, no call_tool seam. T2 may name retrieve_result only as vocabulary data and test fixture.

Design constraints (spec pins no public Go API; keep the seam package-private in internal/service): type resultStore constructed with the T1 config.RetainedResultBounds, an *observe.Logger, an *observe.Metrics, and injectable seams `now func() time.Time` and `entropy io.Reader`; package-private types for namespaces and records (entry / tombstone / marker). Namespace identity is (session id, stamped epoch) or the shared publisher namespace; the store must not read inbound state. Required store operations: a commit that performs per-entry cap check, pre-commit owner/liveness resolution, FIFO entry eviction inside the creating namespace only, the durable 256-byte reservation for each admitted entry, and the hard aggregate admission with exactly the five R10 codes the store owns (result_capacity_exceeded, result_aggregate_capacity_exceeded, result_namespace_retired, result_entropy_unavailable; result_epoch_unresolved is produced by the seam, not the store); a lookup that resolves handle shape then handle resolution and owner binding then page evaluation, returning the shared byte-identical invalid_handle or the typed result_expired / result_evicted; retirement that completes in the trigger commit (funded by its own releases, zero-effect when the namespace holds no live record), leaves a 256-byte tombstone with the R16 half-open lifetime, and makes every later commit/lookup observe the retirement by absent pre-commit owner resolution, never by store bookkeeping; a sweep hook that reclaims memory only (never changes logical results); a born-dead marker discarded at installation. Entry pinning at retention: serialized bytes, the upstream_code bound and its rendered value, ceiling-derived preview/page sizing and handle_ttl/tombstone_ttl deadlines.

Required RED/GREEN tests in internal/service/result_handle_test.go, exactly these names: TestHandleOwnerEpochBinding (AC4), TestHandleExpiry (AC5), TestRetentionBounded (AC7), TestRetiredNamespaceTombstone (AC8), TestHandleRejectionUniformStore (AC16 store half), TestEvictedHandleRetrieval (AC18), TestEvictionNamespaceIsolation (AC36), TestRetirementAdmissionUnconditional (AC38 store half), TestMarkerAdmissionBound (AC39). In internal/observe: TestLogLabelEnumeration (AC13 handler-free runtime closed-registry oracle, both injection paths), TestPagingMetricsRegistered (AC14 registration only; no scrape-delta assertions). Capture the RED state first (compile-failure of the new tests is the required RED), then GREEN. Deterministic fixtures only: injected clock and entropy, no live network, no sleeps for expiry.

Validation, run and report exact output and exit codes: go build ./... ; go test ./internal/service/ -run 'TestHandle|TestRetention|TestMarker|TestEviction|TestRetired|TestRetirement' -count=1 ; go test ./internal/observe/ -count=1 ; gofmt -l on every written file. Do not run the full repository suite. Write .omp/artifacts/receipt_T2.json per the receipt contract. More than 42 read/search operations before your first edit means stop and report stalled; no external SDK/vendor research.
